title: Baby's First Flag
description:
# Welcome to the CTF!

This is your first challenge. The flag is hidden in plain sight.

Hint: The flag format is `flag{...}`.

```
flag{w3lcome_to_the_ctf}
```
hints: Look carefully at the challenge description

title: Robots Aren't Welcome
description:
# Robots.txt

Our web server has some secrets it doesn't want search engines to find.

Check out the target site: `http://challenges.ctf.local:8001`

Can you find what's hidden?
hints: What file tells web crawlers where not to look?

title: Caesar's Cipher
description:
# Caesar Salad

Julius Caesar used a simple substitution cipher. Can you decode this message?

```
synt{pnrfne_jnf_urer}
```

The flag format is `flag{...}`.
hints: ROT13 is a special case of the Caesar cipher
Each letter is shifted by 13 positions

title: Hidden in the Image
description:
# Forensics 101

Something seems off about this image. Can you find the hidden message?

Download the challenge file below.
hints: Have you tried looking at the file's metadata?

title: Who Am I?
description:
# OSINT Challenge

A mysterious developer left a trail online. Their username is `ctf_shadow_2024`.

Find their real location and submit it as the flag in format: `flag{city_country}`.
hints: GitHub profiles sometimes reveal location info

title: XSS Playground
description:
# Cross-Site Scripting

Our latest webapp has a search feature that seems... vulnerable.

Target: `http://challenges.ctf.local:8002`

Find the admin cookie and submit it as the flag.
hints: Try injecting HTML into the search box
script tags might be filtered, but there are other ways...

title: RSA Baby
description:
# RSA Encryption

We intercepted an RSA-encrypted message. The public key parameters seem... weak.

```
n = 323
e = 5
c = 192
```

Decrypt the message and submit it as `flag{plaintext_number}`.
hints: Calculate phi(n) = (p-1)(q-1), then find d such that e*d ≡ 1 mod phi(n)

title: SQL Injection 101
description:
# Login Bypass

The admin panel of this legacy application has a login form.

Can you bypass authentication and retrieve the flag?

Target: `http://challenges.ctf.local:8003`
hints: What happens if you put a single quote in the username field?
